story.title: South Africans Vote in Tense Local Elections Amid Discontent
story.summary: South Africans participated in local government elections on Wednesday, with significant attention on the African National Congress (ANC) amid widespread dissatisfaction over public services, including water shortages and power outages. The elections are seen as a crucial indicator of the national sentiment ahead of future national polls, with the ANC expected to face challenges in retaining support due to ongoing frustrations among voters.

explore_lenses.label: What has changed for the ANC since 2021?
explore_lenses.title: A once-dominant party faces a fragmented field
explore_lenses.summary: The election tests a longer decline in ANC support rather than a single-day shift. The local contest also introduces MK to municipal elections and pits national governing partners ANC and DA against one another in cities.

claims.text: The ANC fell below 50% in municipal voting for the first time in 2021 and lost its parliamentary majority in the 2024 national election, after which it joined a national coalition that includes the DA.

MK, led by former president Jacob Zuma, is contesting a local-government election for the first time; AP reports that it became Parliament's third-largest party in its 2024 debut and has particularly strong support in KwaZulu-Natal.
Ipsos's pre-election survey found the ANC and DA close in Johannesburg and the DA three percentage points ahead in Tshwane; these are survey findings, not results.

explore_lenses.label: Why are service failures central to this vote?
explore_lenses.title: Municipal councils control services voters experience daily
explore_lenses.summary: The complaints in the campaign concern functions that local councils oversee, so the vote directly affects who sets local priorities and administers core services. It does not by itself choose the national government or president.

claims.text: The Electoral Commission says municipal representatives are responsible for improving communities, delivering services, and making and overseeing by-laws; its examples of local services include electricity, water, sanitation, transport and refuse removal.
Voters interviewed by AP in Ekurhuleni and Johannesburg pointed to days without water and broader failures in local conditions as reasons they wanted change.

In Johannesburg, Guardian reporting described voters blaming repeated water and power outages and deteriorated infrastructure, while the city’s governing arrangement involved the ANC, EFF and Patriotic Alliance.

explore_lenses.label: What happens after votes are counted?
explore_lenses.title: Council seat totals will determine coalition bargaining
explore_lenses.summary: Voters elect councillors and party representatives, not mayors directly. Where no party wins a council majority, parties must negotiate support arrangements before the council chooses its leadership.

claims.text: South Africa's Constitution requires municipal electoral systems to produce, in general, proportional representation and permits a combination of party-list proportional representation and ward representation.
Mayors are elected by municipal councils, not directly by voters; an executive mayor requires majority support in the council.

The government’s coalition guidance says there is no predetermined formula for coalition formation: parties negotiate after a hung-council result and before the council’s first meeting to elect office-bearers.

Ipsos analyst Mari Harris forecast that most metropolitan areas could require coalitions if its survey levels were borne out, while cautioning that parties should weigh partners’ governing principles and ability to work together.

story_report.summary: South Africans voted in local government elections on November 2 amid dissatisfaction with public services and infrastructure, including water shortages and power outages. The contest put the African National Congress under renewed pressure, with the party anticipated to receive less than a third of the vote. The immediate stakes were control of municipalities responsible for core local services and the prospect that fragmented council results could require coalition negotiations before mayors are chosen.

sections.heading: ANC losses reshape local contest
sections.body: The ANC fell below 50% in municipal voting for the first time in 2021, then lost its parliamentary majority in the 2024 national election and entered a national coalition that includes the Democratic Alliance. Former president Jacob Zuma’s MK party is contesting a local-government election for the first time; it became Parliament’s third-largest party in its 2024 debut and has particularly strong support in KwaZulu-Natal. An Ipsos survey found the ANC and DA close in Johannesburg and put the DA three points ahead in Tshwane, though those were pre-election findings rather than results.

sections.heading: Service failures drive voter discontent
sections.body: Municipal representatives are responsible for improving communities, delivering services and making and overseeing by-laws. The Electoral Commission identifies electricity, water, sanitation, transport and refuse removal among local services. AP interviews in Ekurhuleni and Johannesburg found voters citing days without water and broader failures in local conditions as reasons for seeking change. Guardian reporting in Johannesburg described voters blaming repeated water and power outages and deteriorating infrastructure; the city’s governing arrangement involved the ANC, EFF and Patriotic Alliance.

sections.heading: Coalition talks could determine mayors
sections.body: South Africa’s Constitution requires municipal electoral systems to produce general proportional representation and permits a mix of party-list and ward representation. Voters do not directly elect mayors: municipal councils do, and an executive mayor needs majority council support. Government coalition guidance says parties negotiate after a hung-council result and before the council’s first meeting to elect office-bearers. Ipsos analyst Mari Harris said most metropolitan areas could require coalitions if survey levels were reflected in voting, while warning that parties must consider prospective partners’ governing principles and ability to work together.

unresolved.text: Final vote and seat totals were not established by election-day reporting or polling, and outcomes may vary sharply by municipality.
Coalition partners, mayoral outcomes and the durability of any governing agreements depend on final results and post-election negotiations.
A change in party control would not by itself establish which level of government caused particular service failures or guarantee how quickly services improve.

related_stories.title: Democrats Gain Control of Congress in Midterm Elections
related_stories.summary: In a significant shift during the 2026 midterm elections, Democrats have regained control of both the House and Senate, marking their first full control of Congress since 2023. This outcome allows them to block President Trump's nominees and influence his agenda. The election results reflect a broader dissatisfaction with Trump's leadership, particularly in light of ongoing issues such as the Iran war.

related_stories.title: Democrats Achieve Significant Wins in Midterm Elections
related_stories.summary: In a notable shift, the Democratic Party secured victories in the U.S. Congress during the midterm elections, marking a significant defeat for the Republican Party and President Donald Trump. Democrats not only retained crucial Senate seats but also won the gubernatorial race in Georgia, indicating a challenging night for Republicans across various regions, including those that traditionally support them.

related_stories.title: Mike Johnson Steps Down as House Republican Leader Following GOP Losses
related_stories.summary: House Speaker Mike Johnson announced he will not continue as the Republican leader in the upcoming Congress after the party's significant losses in the recent elections. This decision was communicated to his staff during a phone call, marking a notable shift in House Republican leadership as they prepare for the new session.
